subject: Target trajectory & sensitivity workstream — kickoff and owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Target trajectory & sensitivity workstream — kickoff and owners

Team —

Kicking off the "Target Trajectory & Sensitivity" workstream that we discussed at the leadership offsite. Goal: produce a short (2–3 page) QBR pack that shows 3 planning targets (Base / Ambitious / Defensive), the underlying assumptions, and sensitivity analyses for the levers we care about (model cost, request growth, latency SLO adherence). This will feed the finance & product targets exercise and the QBR narrative.

Attached: TT-Schedule-v1.pdf (milestones) and budget-scenarios.xlsx (template).

Proposed scope and quick asks:
- Deliverables (by owner):
  - Target trajectories + one-page rationale (owner: Laura)
  - Cost sensitivity matrix (owner: Marcus)
  - Latency/SL A tradeoff scenarios (owner: Mina)
  - Consolidated QBR 2–3 page brief + deck (owner: me / weave)
- Timeline:
  - Aug 1: kickoff (today)
  - Aug 7: draft inputs due from owners
  - Aug 12: internal review with finance and infra
  - Aug 18: leadership dry-run
- Metrics to include: projected monthly token spend, avg p95 latency, throughput headroom, win-rate on pricing conversations (qualitative), and opt-in reduction if we change batching policies.

Decisions we need early: which three model/cost profiles to include (we should pick models that reflect hosted vs dedicated vs private footprints). Marcus — please pick compute cost assumptions and expected quantization savings. Mina — can you model the latency SLO consequences for the defensive target (i.e., more batching + higher latency)?

I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow morning to lock ownership and capture any early blockers. If you can't lead one of the areas above, ping and I will reassign.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Strategy, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com

Attachments: TT-Schedule-v1.pdf, budget-scenarios.xlsx

Thanks, Soojin — good framing. A couple quick notes inline and a proposed tweak.

On Aug 1, 2026, at 08:15, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Kicking off the "Target Trajectory & Sensitivity" workstream...

Proposal: split the sensitivity sheet into two passes —
1) Economic sensitivity (compute price per token, caching effectiveness, request growth) — Marcus lead
2) Operational sensitivity (p95 latency, tail latencies under burst, autoscale lag) — Mina lead

Marcus: can you also produce a simple compute-cost Monte Carlo (5k sims) to show distribution rather than only point estimates? I attached a quick CSV with baseline estimates (compute-model-estimates.csv). If we run a small sim, we can show probability of exceeding budget at different thresholds — that will help sales and finance conversations.

Availability: I can join the Aug 7 draft-review and will block time on the calendar. If useful, I can pull in Engineering Reliability for a short 30m deep-dive on the autoscale tail.

-Vivek
VP, Product & Ops

Attachments: compute-model-estimates.csv

Soojin / Team —

Appreciate the heads-up. From Acme's side we have a couple asks that will affect the defensive scenario:
- Procurement timing: our internal procurement window is Sep 1–15; anything that impacts contract size needs to be flagged by Aug 20.
- Security/compliance: can you confirm which artifacts you'll include for SOC2 / logging retention? Our reviewers will want to see the expected event retention and audit log scope.

Quick answers: we prefer the Base + Defensive scenarios to include a bounded SLA reduction (if applicable) and the estimated impact on per-call success rate. If you can include those lines in the spreadsheet, that will help our legal/procurement teams.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call next week if needed.

—Jessica Park
